note: Real captured pages from the launch retailer, gzipped. Public retailer pages, not customer data. Chosen one per parser case; the facts below were produced by the committed parsers at selection time and are re-asserted by the spec. Amazon fixtures added 2026-09-13 from the PO's second handover package; the search page's session values were redacted on 2026-10-22, the product page is unmodified. Best Buy fixtures added 2026-11-10 from the Best Buy investigation, distilled rather than raw (see each entry's facts.distilled).

fixtures.why: the most populated search page captured

fixtures.name: search-no-results
fixtures.why: embedded state with no Products array — 156 of 271 captured pages

fixtures.name: search-warehouse-id-named-seller
fixtures.why: a warehouse-shaped item id carrying a named third-party seller — the 260-listing case where the id shape and the seller field disagree

fixtures.name: pdp-barcode-empty
fixtures.why: publishes an EMPTY barcode — 91 of 255 captured product pages, and the case that makes an item unverifiable rather than mismatched

fixtures.name: amazon-search-results
fixtures.why: the second retailer's search page — no embedded JSON state, every field parsed from real markup

facts.note: Amazon exposes no seller at the search stage, so isFirstParty is null for all 16 rather than false
facts.redacted: Redacted 2026-10-22 in place (the handover's capture had carried them since 2026-09-13; earlier versions remain in git history): the proxy's anonymous Amazon session id in every encoding it appears in, every anti-CSRF and validation token, a hashed session id, the encrypted slate token and the ad pixel's a2= visitor id, replaced with zeros or REDACTED. The parse was proven identical before and after, and the page carries no api key, zone name, cookie or signed-in customer.

fixtures.name: amazon-search-no-results
fixtures.why: the second retailer's answer to a search nothing matches — the results container (data-component-type="s-search-results"), no result cells, and Amazon's own no-results widget (widgetId=messaging-messages-no-results). Calibrates the line between a results page with nothing on it ([]) and a page that is not a results page at all, or one cut short (null)

facts.redacted: Redacted 2026-10-22 before commit: the proxy's anonymous Amazon session id in every encoding it appears in, every anti-CSRF and validation token, a hashed session id, the encrypted slate token and the ad pixel's a2= visitor id, replaced with zeros or REDACTED. The parse was proven identical before and after, and the page carries no api key, zone name, cookie or signed-in customer.

fixtures.name: amazon-pdp-gtin-labelled
fixtures.why: the barcode is published under "Global Trade Identification Number", NOT "UPC" — the handover's own findings claim every page uses "UPC", and this page is the counter-example. Kept at full size because its 16 incidental "UPC" strings are what the noise control asserts against

fixtures.name: bestbuy-search-upc-first-party
fixtures.why: a barcode search Best Buy answers: the M310 silver's UPC returns one text-matched listing, Best Buy's own

facts.capturedThrough: the vendor, country us, by the Best Buy investigation (row investigate-bestbuy-competitor)
facts.distilled: Distilled by scripts/distil-bestbuy.mjs: only the fields the adapter reads are kept (the GraphQL search and product results, the JSON-LD Product's sku, UPC and seller, and each rendered card's link, title and price), and the adapter's three parsers were proven to give identical output on the raw capture and on this file. Every session value the raw page carried — the vendor's egress addresses in x-forwarded-for, the visitor token, cookies (SID, CTT, __gpi, s_ecid) and analytics ids — is gone by construction, and test/bestbuy-fixtures.spec.ts checks that none remains.
